title: The relative tensor product $\otimes_{\mathcal R}$
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided monoidal category with braiding $\beta$ and with
coequalizers, such that $X\otimes-$ and $-\otimes X$ preserve colimits for every $X$. Let
$\mathcal R$ be a commutative monoid object. For $\mathcal R$-module objects $M$ and $N$,
the *relative tensor product* $M\otimes_{\mathcal R}N$ is the tensor product over
$\mathcal R$ ([lem-sfb-symmetric-bimod-tensor]) of the symmetric bimodules attached to $M$
and $N$ ([lem-sfb-modobj-symmetric-bimodules]), viewed as a left module:
$$
M\otimes_{\mathcal R}N=\operatorname{coeq}\Bigl(M\otimes\mathcal R\otimes N
\rightrightarrows M\otimes N\Bigr)
$$
of $(\gamma_M\beta_{M,\mathcal R})\otimes N$ and $(M\otimes\gamma_N)\alpha_{M,\mathcal R,N}$,
with $\mathcal R$ acting through $M$. With unit the regular module $\mathcal R$, and with
the associator and unitors induced from those of bimodules, this is a monoidal structure
on $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-bimod-monoidal] with $A=\mathcal R$: its hypotheses are exactly the assumed coequalizers and colimit preservation in both variables. Denote its monoidal category by $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Bimod}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ and its tensor by $\odot$. By [lem-sfb-modobj-symmetric-bimodules] there is a fully faithful functor $J\colon\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal B$, sending $M$ to the bimodule with right action $\rho_M=\gamma_M\circ\beta_{M,\mathcal R}$. This fixes both the objects and the morphisms to which the bimodule tensor will be applied.

Define $M\boxtimes N$ to be the left module obtained from $JM\odot JN$ by forgetting its right action. Its underlying object and left action are the coequalizer and the action through $M$ in [lem-sfb-symmetric-bimod-tensor]. Substitute $\rho_M=\gamma_M\circ\beta_{M,\mathcal R}$ from [lem-sfb-modobj-symmetric-bimodules] into the first parallel map; the two maps are exactly the displayed maps defining the relative tensor product. The same tensor lemma says $JM\odot JN$ is symmetric. Thus [def-sfb-symmetric-bimod-module-iso] supplies a bimodule isomorphism $\theta_{M,N}\colon J(M\boxtimes N)\xrightarrow{\sim}JM\odot JN$ whose underlying map and inverse are identities.

source.place: Sentences asserting closure of symmetric bimodules and the identity isomorphism; final sentence identifying the coequalizer.

proof.text: For module maps $f\colon M\to M'$ and $g\colon N\to N'$, define $f\boxtimes g$ by forgetting the right-linearity of $Jf\odot Jg$. This is a left-module map because the tensor in [lem-sfb-bimod-monoidal] is a bimodule morphism. Since the $\theta$ maps above are identities on the underlying objects, one has $\theta_{M',N'}\circ J(f\boxtimes g)=(Jf\odot Jg)\circ\theta_{M,N}$. The identity and composition rules follow from those of the tensor bifunctor in $\mathcal B$, since module maps are determined by their underlying maps, as in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. This defines the tensor bifunctor on module objects.

source.place: Last two sentences: restrict the tensor product to module objects; explicit morphism construction.

proof.text: Take $I=\mathcal R$ with action $\mu$, the regular module of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Its attached right action from [lem-sfb-modobj-symmetric-bimodules] is $\mu\circ\beta_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R}=\mu$ by commutativity of $\mathcal R$. Consequently $JI$ is the regular bimodule, the unit of $\mathcal B$ in [lem-sfb-bimod-monoidal]. No symmetry hypothesis on the ambient braiding has been used.

source.place: Sentence "The regular bimodule R is symmetric because R is commutative".
First two sentences and final two sentences: constraints induced from bimodules; explicit construction instead of invoking transport.

proof.text:
Check naturality, pentagon and triangle using explicit comparison maps. For a parenthesized expression $T$ in module variables and $I$, write $T^{\mathcal B}$ for the expression obtained by replacing each variable $M$ by $JM$, $I$ by $\mathcal R$, and $\boxtimes$ by $\odot$. Define $c_T\colon J(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{\mathcal B}$ by $c_M=1$, $c_I=1$ using step 4, and
$$
c_{U\boxtimes V}=(c_U\odot c_V)\circ\theta_{U,V}.
$$
For module arrows $f\colon U\to U'$ and $g\colon V\to V'$, step 3 and bifunctoriality give
$$
c_{U'\boxtimes V'}\circ J(f\boxtimes g)\circ c_{U\boxtimes V}^{-1}
=(c_{U'}\circ Jf\circ c_U^{-1})\odot(c_{V'}\circ Jg\circ c_V^{-1}).
$$
For composable arrows $h,k$, insertion of $c_T^{-1}c_T=1$ at the intermediate expression gives the conjugate of $J(k\circ h)$ as the composite of their conjugates; identities conjugate to identities. Substituting the composite in step 5 and cancelling its two outer $\theta$ pairs gives
$$
c_{U\boxtimes(V\boxtimes W)}\circ J(a_{U,V,W})\circ c_{(U\boxtimes V)\boxtimes W}^{-1}
=a^{\mathcal B}_{U^{\mathcal B},V^{\mathcal B},W^{\mathcal B}},
$$
where naturality of $a^{\mathcal B}$ moves $c_U,c_V,c_W$ past the middle associator. Substitution of the two unitor composites gives
$$
c_U\circ J(l_U)\circ c_{I\boxtimes U}^{-1}=l^{\mathcal B}_{U^{\mathcal B}},\qquad
c_U\circ J(r_U)\circ c_{U\boxtimes I}^{-1}=r^{\mathcal B}_{U^{\mathcal B}},
$$
using naturality of the bimodule unitors. Applying the tensor and composition formulas to the five edges of the module pentagon identifies its two paths with the two paths of the bimodule pentagon. Applying them to the triangle identifies its associator followed by $1\boxtimes l$ with the bimodule associator followed by $1\odot l^{\mathcal B}$, and its $r\boxtimes1$ path with $r^{\mathcal B}\odot1$. These paths agree by [lem-sfb-bimod-monoidal]. For naturality, step 3 gives natural $\theta$; composing its naturality equations with those for the bimodule associator and each unitor gives naturality of the three composites in step 5. Finally, equality of the resulting underlying maps is equality of module morphisms by [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Thus the displayed relative tensor and regular unit satisfy all monoidal axioms.

source.place: Last two sentences: full verification of the asserted monoidal structure.
